doe-osti-17070149-stability-analysis-for:
Khanh Nguyen, YuHsiang Lan, Paul Fischer, and colleagues at Argonne National Laboratory checked a magnetohydrodynamics solver in report ANL-26/49. The solver, part of Nek5000/RS, models electrically conducting fluids under magnetic fields. Their test case is steady flow in a square duct with conducting walls of varied thickness.

Linear stability math predicts how fast small wobbles in the flow should grow, for Hartmann numbers from 30 to 500 and Reynolds numbers in the thousands. Full simulations in the code matched those predicted growth rates. At a fixed wall conductance ratio, thicker walls made the flow more unstable. The match gives users a verified benchmark for unsteady MHD work.
